chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not merely another No.1 Trainer title. It is the senior-track final-stage domestic champion route, where the trophy card reportedly shifts from regional non-holo credential into a Holofoil photo-bearing Best in Japan object.

key_artists.why: Sugimori matters because the trophy lineage borrows the visual authority of early Pokemon itself: the same artist bound to Satoshi Tajiri, the original game artwork, and the redrawn Generation I watercolor language becomes the face of a competitive credential.

claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place prize source group as one row containing No.1 Trainer at source index 199.
Bulbapedia says No.1 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a first-place prize in the Pokémon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says top-ranking players from Secret Super Battle were eligible to compete in a Best in Japan Deciding Match in late August 2000, while overall winners of Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented Japan in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii.
Pokumon places the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan Deciding Match at Pokémon Center Tokyo in Tokyo, Japan on August 19, 2000.
Bulbapedia says winners of the Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.1 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration.

Pokumon reports that winners of the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan event received No.1-3 Trainer trophy cards, that each is reported to be cosmos holofoil with the winner's photograph printed onto it, and that no photos have surfaced to confirm that report.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.1 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokémon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use.

Pokumon says World Challenge Summer 2000 separated Tropical Mega Battle for players aged 14 or under from Secret Super Battle for players 15+, supporting the senior-track boundary for this Best in Japan route.

This first-place Best in Japan card must be separated from regional Secret Super Battle No.1 Trainer cards, which Bulbapedia describes as Non Holofoil, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male/female Trainer versions.

Agents must identify this as the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place route before using No.1 Trainer value, rarity, or lore. The special rail must preserve final-stage senior-track context, Holofoil/photo-trophy signals, and boundaries against regional SSB, TMB/Hawaii, Worlds, Challenge Road, Lizardon/Kamex, Neo Road, Battle Road, and name-only No.1 Trainer claims.

As judged collector texture, the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan No.1 Trainer matters because it turns a final domestic senior champion into a card-object: rank, route, venue, trophy lineage, and reportedly the player's photograph all compressed into a single unnumbered promo.
not_claiming: that reported photograph details are enough to identify a specific seller card

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer [SSB Best in Japan]: the senior champion made photographic
narrative.why_it_matters: This is where No.1 Trainer stops being only a rank and becomes a person standing inside the card. The route matters: not the regional non-holo SSB prize, not the junior Tropical Mega Battle path to Hawaii, but the senior Best in Japan final at Pokemon Center Tokyo. Bulbapedia gives the Holofoil photograph-superimposed story; Pokumon adds the more fragile collector note that the cards are reported as cosmos photo trophies, while no photos have surfaced to confirm the report. That tension is exactly why the catalog needs special identification instructions: the beauty is in the assembly, and the assembly has to be read before the name can mean anything.
not_claiming: that every No.1 Trainer listing uses this same route
that reported photo-trophy details alone authenticate a listing

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.1 Trainer, World Challenge, Secret Super Battle, Best in Japan, senior division, 15+, Pokemon Center Tokyo, Holofoil, cosmos, winner photograph, printed photo, superimposed photo, Tropical Mega Battle, Hawaii, or World Exchange Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.1 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.1 Trainer / Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place prize, not regional Secret Super Battle, Tropical Mega Battle, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships, or name-only No.1 Trainer.
Preserve the senior-track split: Pokumon describes Secret Super Battle as the 15+ track and Tropical Mega Battle as the 14-or-under track.
Preserve the finals venue and date as a source-backed route clue: Pokumon places Secret Super Battle Best in Japan at Pokemon Center Tokyo on August 19, 2000.

Separate this final-stage card from regional Secret Super Battle No.1 Trainer cards. Regional SSB cards are described as Non Holofoil, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and route to the Best in Japan machinery rather than being the Best in Japan champion card itself.

Treat Holofoil, cosmos holofoil, winner photograph, superimposed photograph, and printed photograph as important route clues, but not as authentication. Bulbapedia and Pokumon differ in detail and Pokumon notes that no photos have surfaced to confirm the reported SSB finals photo cards.

Do not treat the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle story as this card's route. Bulbapedia assigns the Hawaii representative path to Tropical Mega Battle regional winners, not Secret Super Battle Best in Japan.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including full front/back, Holofoil/photo area, any name or rank text, edges, surface, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that No.1 Trainer name alone identifies the exact print
that Holofoil or photo claims alone authenticate the card
that a grading label alone resolves the route

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 199 as No.1 Trainer from the World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place prize slice.
Bulbapedia gives the Japanese name as Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and describes No.1 Trainer as a Japanese tournament Trainer/Item card lineage used for first-place prizes.
Bulbapedia says winners of the Best in Japan finals were awarded Holofoil No.1 Trainer cards bearing their photograph superimposed on the illustration.

Pokumon identifies this No.1 Trainer as a World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan 2000 Japanese unnumbered Trainer Winner card illustrated by Ken Sugimori, with cosmos holofoil treatment and an estimated copy count of one; this dossier treats the copy count as a collector estimate, not official disclosure.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.1 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori; Pokumon also labels this Best in Japan No.1 Trainer card with Ken Sugimori.

As interpretive art context, Sugimori's credit matters because a final-stage tournament trophy card borrows the franchise's original visual authority while turning a real player result into a collectible object.

This card must be separated from World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional No.1 Trainer, World Challenge Tropical Mega Battle No.1 Trainer, World Exchange Battle/Hawaii route cards, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships No.1 Trainer, and name-only No.1 Trainer listings.

As judged collector texture, No.1 Trainer [World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first place] is the senior final winner becoming a card: the rank is printed, the route is legible, and the reported photo treatment makes the human victory difficult to separate from the object.

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer: the final senior winner inside the card
narrative.why_it_matters: The No.1 title is loud, but the quiet part is the route. This is the Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place card: older-player circuit, final domestic stage, Pokemon Center Tokyo, and a trophy form that sources describe through Holofoil and winner-photograph language. It is exactly the sort of card where the catalog should slow the agent down. First read the assembly. Then read the card.
not_claiming: that every No.1 Trainer print follows this route
that catalog identity makes evidence spendable

special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this card by exact final-stage senior route, Holofoil/photo trophy signals, and Best in Japan context, not by the reusable No.1 Trainer title.
steps: Confirm the title No.1 Trainer / Ｎｏ.１トレーナー and the exact route World Challenge Secret Super Battle Best in Japan first-place prize.
Check whether the listing or image claims Holofoil, cosmos holofoil, a winner photograph, a superimposed photograph, or a printed photograph. Treat these as final-stage clues, not authentication.
Separate from regional Secret Super Battle No.1 Trainer cards, which are described as Non Holofoil and personalized with winner name and regional conference.
Separate from Tropical Mega Battle and the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle path. Similar World Challenge language does not mean the same lane.
Separate from Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, World Championships, and generic No.1 Trainer listings.

If the card is graded, record the slab label but do not let the label alone resolve the route. Ask for front/back photos, Holofoil/photo area, any name/rank text, surface, edges, and slab cert imagery.
Keep the source caveat visible: Pokumon reports cosmos photo trophies and notes no surfaced photos to confirm that report, while Bulbapedia gives broader Holofoil/photo-superimposed finals wording.
